title: SharePoint: eSignature recipient groups let any one of up to 10 people sign for a slot
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout, default state and recipient-group behaviour match Microsoft's notice. The existing eSignature controls, per-request pricing and audit search details are supported by Microsoft Learn; the remaining group-specific questions are accurately identified as undocumented.

claims.quote: We are introducing recipient groups for eSignature in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn's cited eSignature pages do not describe recipient groups as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: eSignature recipient groups sharing links notifications external guests audit events automated signing; opened eSignature setup, overview, Word request, PDF request and troubleshoot pages. No recipient-group documentation found.

claims.quote: At least one required signature field is needed for each recipient.

claims.claim: Microsoft presents recipient groups as reducing delays when a specific signer is unavailable.
claims.quote: This update helps make signature workflows more reliable by reducing delays when a specific signer is unavailable

claims.claim: An eSignature request is a record of agreement.
claims.quote: The eSignature service enables binding agreements between parties.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An administrator must set up eSignature in the Microsoft 365 admin center before it can be used, including in tenants wanting recipient groups.

claims.claim: Which recipient-group members receive the sharing link, and when, is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: eSignature recipient groups sharing links notifications external guests audit events automated signing; opened setup, overview, Word request and PDF request pages. They describe recipient links but not group-member delivery or timing.

claims.claim: Requesting signatures from external recipients who are not existing guests requires Microsoft Entra B2B integration for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.quote: Searched: eSignature recipient groups sharing links notifications external guests audit events automated signing; opened setup, overview, Word request, PDF request and troubleshoot pages. External recipients are covered, but recipient-group membership is not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Conditional Access can prevent external eSignature signers from opening documents or completing signatures.
claims.quote: external signers might not be able to access and read the document for signing. In some other cases, they might be able to access the document for signing, but the signing operation is unsuccessful.

claims.claim: Learn identifies adding eSignature, formerly Microsoft eSignature Service, to approved apps through the Microsoft Entra admin center as one common Conditional Access remedy.
claims.quote: One common way to resolve this issue is to add eSignature (formally called Microsoft eSignature Service) to the list of approved apps via the Microsoft Entra admin center.

claims.claim: The feature description concerns people signing and does not describe automated or agent signing.
claims.quote: Searched: eSignature recipient groups sharing links notifications external guests audit events automated signing; read MC1290821 and opened setup, overview, Word request and PDF request pages. No automated or agent signing for recipient groups was described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: eSignature recipient groups sharing links notifications external guests audit events automated signing; opened setup, overview, Word request and PDF request pages. General notifications and link expiration are described, not post-signing group-member behaviour.
